title: Scripture as Final Authority
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Scripture as final authority means that God’s written Word stands above all human opinion, tradition, experience, culture, emotion, and spiritual claims. Because Scripture is God’s Word, it has the final say over doctrine, obedience, worship, correction, and the life of the church.
summary: Scripture as final authority means that God’s written Word stands above all human opinion, tradition, experience, culture, emotion, and spiritual claims. Because Scripture is God’s Word, it has the final say over doctrine, obedience, worship, correction, and the life of the church.
christFocus: Jesus Christ lived under the authority of Scripture, fulfilled Scripture, and resisted temptation with Scripture. To follow Christ faithfully is to receive the Word of God as the final authority over every part of life.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
God’s people need a final authority because many voices compete for trust. Personal feelings, cultural pressure, religious traditions, popular teachers, spiritual experiences, and human wisdom may all claim authority, but none of them stand above the Word of God.

Scripture as final authority does not mean believers reject wisdom, counsel, history, or faithful teaching. It means all of those things must be tested by God’s Word. No teacher, church, tradition, movement, or personal experience has the right to overrule what God has spoken.

Jesus Himself treated Scripture as binding and trustworthy. He answered temptation by saying, “It is written,” and He taught that God’s Word would not fail. He did not place Himself against Scripture but fulfilled it perfectly.

The church remains faithful only as it stands under Scripture. When Scripture is treated as optional, adjustable, or secondary, the people of God become vulnerable to error, manipulation, compromise, and spiritual drift.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
People are often pressured to choose between God’s Word and the approval of others. Some are told to follow their heart, trust their feelings, accept cultural trends, or obey religious authorities without question. Scripture as final authority gives believers a firm foundation when every other voice shifts.

This doctrine protects the wounded and the confused from being ruled by powerful personalities or spiritual manipulation. It reminds every believer that God has spoken clearly enough to be trusted and authoritatively enough to be obeyed.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring every belief, desire, decision, teaching, and spiritual claim under Scripture. Do not ask first whether something is popular, emotional, traditional, or personally appealing; ask whether it agrees with the Word of God. Let Scripture correct you where you are wrong, steady you where you are afraid, and lead you into faithful obedience to Christ.
